# gitlabcommits Provider

The gitlabcommits provider manages files on GitLab branches through the GitLab Commits API. Each create, update or destroy of a gitlabcommits_files resource makes a maximum of one commit, with all its file changes. A replacement can make two commits in one apply: a delete commit and a create commit.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    gitlabcommits = {
      source = "greeddj/gitlabcommits"
      # Pin the provider version, for example:
      # version = "~> 0.3.0"
    }
  }
}

# You can set the token and the GitLab URL in GITLAB_TOKEN and GITLAB_BASE_URL.
# Then you do not need this provider block.
provider "gitlabcommits" {
  token    = var.gitlab_token
  base_url = "https://gitlab.com" # This is the default. For a self-managed GitLab, set its URL.
}

variable "gitlab_token" {
  description = "GitLab token: an access token with the api scope, or a fine-grained personal access token. See Authentication on the provider page."
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
}
```

## Authentication

The provider needs a GitLab token for the REST API. Use one of these token
types:

- A project or group access token with the `api` scope.
- A personal access token with the `api` scope. On GitLab.com, a top-level
  group can enforce fine-grained tokens. After the enforcement date, its
  projects refuse personal access tokens that are not fine-grained. They
  continue to accept project, group and service account tokens.
- A fine-grained personal access token (GitLab 19.2 and later) with these
  permissions on the project or on its group:
  - `Commit: Create`, `Repository: Read`, `Branch: Read` and `Project: Read`.
  - `Branch: Create`, if a resource sets `create_branch_from`.

The `write_repository`, `read_api` and `read_repository` scopes do not let the
provider make commits. For the data sources, `read_api` is enough.

To make commits, the user of the token needs the Developer role or a higher
role. For a project or group access token, this is the bot user of the token.
A protected branch accepts commits only from the roles in its "Allowed to push
and merge" setting. The default value is "Maintainers".

Set the token in `token` or in the `GITLAB_TOKEN` environment variable. Set the
GitLab URL in `base_url` or in `GITLAB_BASE_URL`. The provider uses the
argument first. If the argument is null or an empty string, the provider uses
the environment variable.

Terraform must know the values of all provider arguments when it configures
the provider. If an argument gets its value from a resource, first apply that
resource with `terraform apply -target`.

Make sure that you set `base_url` or `GITLAB_BASE_URL` for a self-managed
GitLab. If you do not set one of them, the provider sends the token to
`https://gitlab.com`.

Do not write the token in Terraform files that you keep in a Git repository.
In CI/CD, use `GITLAB_TOKEN` or a sensitive variable.

The provider refuses a CI job token, for example the value of `CI_JOB_TOKEN`
or a token that starts with `glcbt-`. A job token cannot make commits through
the API.

## Limits

- **Commit request size.** All changes of a resource go into one commit
  request. GitLab refuses a request larger than 300 MB (the default).
- **Retries and rate limits.** The provider retries a read after HTTP 429, HTTP
  5xx (except 501) or some connection errors. After HTTP 429, it waits at least
  the time that GitLab asks for. If GitLab asks for more than 5 minutes or
  gives no time, the wait starts at `retry_wait_min_ms` and doubles after each
  retry.
- **A failed commit request.** A second request can make a second commit. So
  the provider retries a commit request only after HTTP 429, or after a
  connection error before it sends the request. If a failed request possibly
  made a commit, the error tells you what to do. If GitLab made the commit:
  - With `adopt_existing = true` (the default), a later apply adopts the
    created files without a new commit. After an update, this needs
    `detect_drift = true` in state. With `adopt_existing = false`, that apply
    fails because these files exist.
  - After a failed destroy, run `terraform destroy` again. It skips the deleted
    files.
- **Timeouts, redirects and proxies.** A request waits at most 5 minutes for
  the response headers. An upload or a download has no time limit. The
  provider does not follow a redirect to another host, or from `https` to
  `http`. It uses `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY`, but has no setting
  for timeouts, CA certificates, client certificates or TLS verification.
- **A Gitaly error that looks like a missing file.** GitLab can answer HTTP 404
  for a file that exists when Gitaly, its Git storage service, does not answer
  in time. The provider does not always find such an error. Then:
  - A refresh can remove the file from state. The next apply adopts the file
    again, or fails if `adopt_existing = false`.
  - A destroy, or an update that deletes the file, can leave the file on the
    branch.
  - For a new path, the apply can create a file at the path of a directory.
    GitLab then deletes the directory and all files in it.
- **A branch with the name of a tag.** The provider does not support such a
  branch, because GitLab then uses the tag. A refresh can remove files from
  state, a destroy can leave files on the branch, and commits can fail. Rename
  or delete the tag.
- **Git LFS.** Do not use the provider to change the content of an LFS-tracked
  file. GitLab puts a file in Git LFS only when a commit creates it, so an
  update takes the file out of LFS with no warning.
  - The provider and the `gitlabcommits_file` data source get only the LFS
    pointer of such a file. A pointer to the configured content counts as the
    same content. For a pointer to other content, an error or a warning tells
    you what to do.
  - To change an LFS-tracked file, use git and Git LFS. Then set the new
    content in `files`, with `detect_drift = true` (the default) in state. With
    `false`, the apply fails or commits a regular file. See
    [Values from the last apply](resources/files.md#values-from-the-last-apply).
- **Text in an encoding other than UTF-8.** GitLab changes text in another
  encoding, for example UTF-16, to UTF-8 before the provider reads it. So an
  adoption can try to update a file that already contains the configured
  bytes. State and the `gitlabcommits_file` data source can also
  contain the UTF-8 text. To keep the encoding, set `content_base64` to the
  base64 form of the bytes on the branch.
- **Unicode normalization (NFC).** Terraform changes all strings, also the keys
  of `files`, to the NFC form. The provider cannot manage a path that the
  repository stores in another form, for example NFD. The apply creates a
  second file with the NFC name. For text that must keep another form, use
  `content_base64`.

## Schema

### Optional

- `base_url` (String) The URL of the GitLab instance, with or without /api/v4, for example https://gitlab.example.com. If base_url is null or empty, the provider uses GITLAB_BASE_URL, or https://gitlab.com if neither has a value. See the provider page, Authentication.
- `max_retries` (Number) The maximum number of retries of a failed GitLab request, from 0 to 100. The default is 5, and 0 stops all retries. See the provider page, Limits.
- `retry_wait_max_ms` (Number) After HTTP 429, the provider adds a random time to each wait, from 0 to retry_wait_max_ms minus retry_wait_min_ms milliseconds. This value does not limit the wait. It must be from 1 to 3600000 and not less than retry_wait_min_ms, with a default of 30000.
- `retry_wait_min_ms` (Number) The minimum wait in milliseconds before a retry after HTTP 429, from 1 to 3600000. The default is 1000, and the value must not be more than retry_wait_max_ms. See the provider page, Limits.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The GitLab access token. A fine-grained token needs Commit: Create, Repository: Read, Branch: Read and Project: Read, and also Branch: Create if you set create_branch_from. If token is null or empty, the provider uses GITLAB_TOKEN. See the provider page, Authentication.
